title: add offline operator bundle with distro shims and explicit dependency graph
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Added an air-gapped operator bundle that includes distro-specific shims and an explicit dependency graph for deterministic offline installs. No breaking changes. Backwards compatible with existing seed registry layouts.
description:
Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private into strict air-gapped and heterogeneous on-prem fleets have asked for a single, verifiable operator bundle that carries OS-specific shims and a machine-readable dependency graph so site admins can pre-seed registries deterministically. This PR introduces an "offline operator bundle" artifact plus supporting installer changes.

Motivation: reduce manual steps when installing in regulated environments, make preflight verification deterministic, and provide safe rollback hooks for operator-driven components.

Changes in this PR include:
1) packaging: add 'bundles/offline-operator' containing:
 - operator-manifests.yaml (CRDs + controller manifests, rendered for non-rootless installs)
 - distro-shims/{ubuntu20.04,ubuntu22.04,almalinux9,rocky8}.yaml that patch nodeSelector/tolerations and initContainers required for kernel-module preload or real-time variants
 - dependency-graph.yaml (simple DAG mapping images -> checksums -> seed-order)
 - checksums.txt and image-list.csv for registry seeding automation
2) installer: installer/airgap/verify_bundle.go and a lightweight verifier script installer/airgap/bin/verify-bundle that validates checksums, ensures distro shim compatibility, and emits a seed order for registries
3) helm: charts/private/Chart.yaml and templates updated to support an optional OperatorDeployment that will be deployed from the offline bundle and is annotated for safe-rollbacks
4) terraform: modules/registry-seed added support for the explicit seed order and an atomic 'seed-plan' input consumed by the registry sync job
5) upgrade/rollback: installer/airgap/rollback-metadata.json is emitted by the installer to allow deterministic reversal to the previous operator bundle.

Checklist:
 - [x] bundle produced by CI artifact pipeline
 - [x] verify-bundle tool + unit tests
 - [x] terraform module consumed by local e2e seed runner
 - [x] helm templates include canary labels and rollback annotations
 - [x] docs updated (quickstart airgap section)

Commits summary:
 - add offline bundle layout and assets
 - implement verify-bundle CLI and unit tests
 - wire verify step into installer preflight
 - helm chart: operator deployment and rollback annotations
 - terraform: seed-plan ingestion and example
 - docs: airgap quickstart and operator bundle explanation

Files changed (high level):
 - bundles/offline-operator/operator-manifests.yaml
 - bundles/offline-operator/distro-shims/ubuntu22.04.yaml
 - bundles/offline-operator/dependency-graph.yaml
 - installer/airgap/verify_bundle.go
 - installer/airgap/bin/verify-bundle
 - installer/airgap/rollback-metadata.json
 - charts/private/templates/operator-deployment.yaml
 - terraform/modules/registry-seed/main.tf
 - terraform/examples/seed-plan/seed-plan.yaml
 - docs/airgap/operator-bundle.md
 - Makefile (CI targets)
 - ci/publish-bundle.yml

Testing performed: unit tests for verifier (checksum and DAG validation), integration run against a local registry seeded by terraform example (seed-plan), cluster smoke test deploying operator from bundle to K3s 1.26 and RKE2 1.22, manual validation on AlmaLinux and Ubuntu 22.04 nodes for shim behavior.

Backwards compatibility notes: the bundle format is additive; older installers ignore the new dependency-graph.yaml and distro-shims, so legacy installs are unaffected.

Migration: for existing airgap customers, recommended flow is to run verify-bundle --generate-seed-plan and feed the resulting seed-plan to the terraform registry-seed module; the installer will then apply the operator as an optional step.

Rollback story: the installer writes rollback-metadata.json before switching operator versions; running installer/airgap/rollback --from-file rollback-metadata.json will atomically revert operator deployment and return registry seeds to previous checksums where possible.

CI: some flakiness observed on the integration job that pulls from a transient local registry; reran twice and green on second attempt.

Security/Signoff: added checksum verification to prevent accidental divergent images; reviewers audited shims to avoid escalation vectors in initContainers.

Docs: docs/airgap/operator-bundle.md describes the bundle layout and step-by-step seed-plan generation.

Operational notes:
 - seed-plan is intentionally explicit to enable customers to copy seed order to offline registries that do not support dependency graphs
 - distro-shims are lightweight and only patch nodeAffinity/tolerations and an optional initContainer; they do not introduce privileged mounts by default

Rollout plan: merge into main, tag v0.11.0-bundle, publish bundle artifact to CI storage, send migration guide to customers who opted in to operator-managed installs.

Related work: ENG-2147 (airgap improvements), ENG-2203 (installer rollback metadata).

implement verify-bundle CLI with checksum/DAG validation

notes_for_release: v0.11.0-bundle: adds offline operator bundle, distro shims, explicit dependency graph, verifier tool, terraform seed-plan support, and rollback metadata. See docs/airgap/operator-bundle.md for migration steps.
guidance_for_ops: Use verify-bundle to produce an ordered seed-plan and run terraform/examples/seed-plan with the registry-seed module. Keep rollback-metadata.json safe until installation validated. For air-gapped customers on mixed distro fleets, prefer distro-specific shims to avoid nodeSelector drift.
